subject: Chemistry
q: For the Balmer series of hydrogen, the wavenumber is ν̄ = R_H(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²). Consider the statements: (I) as wavelength decreases, successive lines converge; (II) n₁ = 2; (III) the longest-wavelength line has n₂ = 3; (IV) the ionization energy of ground-state hydrogen can be obtained directly from the wavenumbers of these Balmer lines. Which statements are correct?
hint: In the Balmer series the lower level is fixed at n = 2, and the smallest energy gap occurs for the 3 → 2 transition.
solution: For every Balmer line, n₁ = 2 and n₂ = 3, 4, 5, … . The longest wavelength corresponds to the smallest transition energy, so n₂ = 3. As n₂ increases, the wavelengths decrease and the lines approach the series limit, so they converge. Balmer-line wavenumbers describe transitions ending at n = 2; they do not directly give the ground-state (n = 1) ionization energy. Therefore statements (I), (II) and (III) are correct.
